title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to protect election integrity by establishing safeguards against AI-generated misinformation. It sets up regulations and penalties for individuals or groups that use AI to deceive voters or manipulate electoral processes.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives states that Congress should refuse to give additional funding or special regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency due to acute stress in the AI market. Instead, it urges that support be directed toward all Americans who have been harmed by these developments.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes rules to make AI research more trustworthy and reliable. It requires developers to rigorously test AI systems, document their methods, and share findings so the public can rely on their safety and effectiveness.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for the Department of Veterans Affairs to use and disclose artificial intelligence systems, ensuring clear labeling of AI components in its services. It aims to protect veterans by making AI decision‑making transparent, fostering trust, accountability, and compliance with ethical standards.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes rules to ensure that any artificial‑intelligence systems used by the Department of Veterans Affairs to evaluate and process veterans’ claims are transparent, fair, and reliable. It requires the VA to regularly audit these AI tools, disclose their decision‑making logic, and provide clear avenues for veterans to challenge or appeal decisions made with AI assistance.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to shield consumers from misleading or manipulative AI technologies. It establishes rules that require AI developers to be transparent about how their systems work, provide clear disclosures, and hold themselves accountable for any deceptive practices.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to establish guidelines and requirements to ensure AI systems are secure and resilient against potential threats. It mandates the development of security standards, risk assessment protocols, and compliance measures for organizations deploying advanced AI technologies.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes creating a CISA‑led task force to protect the nation’s AI systems from cyber threats and ensure they are built and operated securely. It calls for coordinated monitoring, risk assessment, and collaboration between government, industry, and experts to strengthen AI resilience and safeguard critical infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 aims to create a comprehensive framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with artificial intelligence technologies. It establishes regulatory standards, oversight mechanisms, and security safeguards to ensure AI systems are developed and deployed safely, transparently, and responsibly.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes rules for how AI‑controlled machines—such as robots, autonomous vehicles, and drones—must work together safely and reliably. It creates standards, oversight mechanisms, and coordination procedures to ensure that these physical AI systems comply with safety, privacy, and accountability requirements.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by curbing the use of AI-generated content that could mislead voters. It proposes transparency requirements, safeguards, and enforcement measures to detect and counter deceptive AI campaigns.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes a framework for tracking and regulating artificial intelligence systems that can learn and adapt on their own, ensuring they remain safe and aligned with human values. It requires developers to disclose updates, maintain oversight, and provide transparency to regulators to prevent unintended consequences.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act seeks to prevent the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems that could pose serious threats to public safety. It proposes strict regulatory measures, including mandatory safety testing, transparency requirements, and penalties for non‑compliance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on the construction and operation of new AI data centers. It aims to curb rapid expansion of these facilities to address environmental and societal concerns.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board tasked with examining cybersecurity and artificial intelligence incidents and threats. The board will investigate such incidents, recommend actions, and help safeguard national security and public safety from AI and cyber risks.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act seeks to ensure that artificial intelligence technologies are developed and deployed in ways that benefit American citizens. It likely includes provisions for boosting AI innovation, safeguarding privacy and ethics, and making AI tools accessible and useful across industries.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act establishes a systematic framework for monitoring how artificial intelligence affects China’s political, economic, and social power dynamics. It mandates regular assessments and reporting to ensure AI technologies align with national interests and governance objectives.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that bars artificial‑intelligence systems from diagnosing or treating patients, reserving these medical functions solely for licensed human doctors. The act is designed to safeguard patient safety, ensure accountability, and uphold professional standards in healthcare.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The proposed policy creates a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President. It is intended to identify, assess, and coordinate responses to risks posed by AI and other emerging technologies across the federal government.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI policy, governance, and ethical considerations. The committee will review AI initiatives, recommend regulations, and ensure responsible use of AI technology.
